longest transaction = 264ms (threshold 2000ms)
lock held was ShareUpdateExclusiveLock only, no query regression (0 seq-scanned rows before/after)

evidence: max writer stall 3ms (threshold 50ms)
longest transaction 91ms (threshold 2000ms)
constraint_validated_inline_on_populated_table=false, query plans unchanged (0 seq-scanned rows before/after)

review.summary: Adding the NOT NULL column with a volatile clock_timestamp() default rewrites/locks the 1M-row orders table and stalls the concurrent writer for ~509ms under an AccessExclusiveLock (longest txn ~520ms) — replace it with an add-nullable-then-batched-backfill-then-validate pattern.
evidence: Original migration: concurrent writer max stall ~509ms (threshold 50ms), longest transaction ~520ms holding AccessExclusiveLock on orders
Verified fix: longest transaction 102ms, max writer stall 2ms, 0 lock_timeout errors
verify_fix confirms schema_equivalent=true and clean_under_thresholds=true, with identical NOT NULL + DEFAULT clock_timestamp() end state and no query regression (0 rows seq-scanned before/after)
review.action: Replace the single ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp() statement with the verified add-nullable/backfill-in-batches/validate-then-SET NOT NULL sequence before deploying.

review.summary: ALTER COLUMN TYPE bigint rewrites the whole 1M-row orders table under AccessExclusiveLock, stalling concurrent writers for 465ms — replace with an additive column + batched backfill + swap.
evidence: Original migration: writer max_stall_ms=465 (threshold 50ms), single transaction 465ms holding AccessExclusiveLock
Fixed migration: writer max_stall_ms=13ms, longest transaction 68ms
verify_fix confirms schema_equivalent=true and clean_under_thresholds=true
review.action: Replace the direct ALTER COLUMN TYPE with the additive-column-plus-batched-backfill-and-swap migration before deploying.

review.summary: Plain CREATE INDEX on orders(status) takes a ShareLock that stalls concurrent writers for 213ms, well above the 50ms threshold.
evidence: writer max_stall_ms=213 with plain CREATE INDEX vs 2ms with CONCURRENTLY
locks_held_on_user_tables: orders ShareLock (plain) vs ShareUpdateExclusiveLock (CONCURRENTLY)
verify_fix: schema_equivalent=true, clean_under_thresholds=true
review.fixed_migration: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_status_idx ON orders (status);
review.action: Replace CREATE INDEX with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (run outside a transaction block) to avoid blocking writers.

review.summary: The single-statement UPDATE backfilling 1M rows runs as one 3.5s transaction and stalls the concurrent writer for up to 3.3s, exceeding both the transaction-duration and writer-stall thresholds.
evidence: longest_transaction_ms=3494 (threshold 2000ms)
concurrent writer max_stall_ms=3300 (threshold 50ms)
fix reduced longest_transaction_ms to 22 and max_stall_ms to 2 with schema_equivalent=true
review.action: Replace the single UPDATE with the batched DO-block backfill (5000 rows/commit) to keep transactions short and writer stalls under 50ms.

review.summary: ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN notes irreversibly destroys the notes data for the ~10% of orders that have it (99,769 rows in the 1M-row shadow set), which is an automatic DATA_LOSS hazard regardless of low writer stall or query impact.
evidence: simulate_migration reports dropped_columns: ["orders.notes"] with 0 lossy_changes reported but the column and its data are gone (not recoverable)
99,769 of 1,000,000 orders rows had non-null notes in the seeded data (~10%), all lost by DROP COLUMN
Writer stall (3ms) and transaction time (0ms) are fine, but that is irrelevant because DATA_LOSS outranks LOCK_BLOCKING/QUERY_REGRESSION per the hazard precedence rules
review.action: Do not run the drop as-is; first archive orders.notes (e.g. into orders_notes_backup or an export) for all non-null rows, get sign-off that the archived data satisfies retention needs, then run the DROP COLUMN — note that verify_fix correctly reports schema_equivalent:false because a data-preserving fix necessarily leaves an extra backup table, which is the expected and required trade-off versus silent data loss.

review.summary: ALTER COLUMN email TYPE varchar(20) USING left(email,20) silently truncates 10,001 of 20,000 existing emails (max length 21) and can also introduce duplicate values violating the UNIQUE constraint — do not run as written.
evidence: simulate_migration: lossy_changes reports 'longest existing value was 21 chars; column is now varchar(20)'
run_sql: 10001 of 20000 customers.email rows exceed 20 chars (max=21)
verify_fix (guarded rewrite) errors out safely with 'Cannot narrow customers.email to varchar(20): 10001 existing rows exceed 20 characters', proving truncation is unavoidable without data cleanup
review.action: Do not deploy this migration; instead have the DBA/product decide how to handle the 10,001 emails longer than 20 characters (truncate deliberately with dedup handling, widen the UI limit, or store the full email elsewhere) before any column narrowing is attempted.

review.summary: Adding the FK inline validates it against all 1M existing orders rows, blocking writers (79ms stall, ShareRowExclusiveLock) — use NOT VALID + VALIDATE CONSTRAINT instead.
evidence: constraint_validated_inline_on_populated_table:true, writer max_stall_ms:79 (>50ms threshold)
Original migration held ShareRowExclusiveLock on orders/customers during inline validation
Fixed version (NOT VALID then VALIDATE) reduced writer stall to 2ms and used only ShareUpdateExclusiveLock, schema_equivalent:true
review.fixed_migration:
ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_fkey2 FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers (id) NOT VALID;
ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_fkey2;
review.action: Replace the inline FK addition with ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID followed by a separate VALIDATE CONSTRAINT statement.

review.summary: Dropping orders_customer_id_idx is not actually unused — it causes recent_orders_for_customer to fall back to a full sequential scan.
evidence: After DROP INDEX, query plan changed from Bitmap Index Scan (0 seq rows, 0.044ms) to Seq Scan over 1,000,002 rows (13.24ms) — a ~300x slowdown, far past the 100k row / 5x thresholds
Migration itself is fast (2ms) and writer stall stayed low (4ms), so the lock behavior is fine — the hazard is purely the query regression
Fix (add covering index (customer_id, created_at DESC) CONCURRENTLY before dropping old index) verified clean: seq_scanned=0, execution 0.017ms, writer stall 2ms, longest txn 282ms
review.fixed_migration:
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_customer_created_idx ON orders (customer_id, created_at DESC);
DROP INDEX orders_customer_id_idx;
review.action: Before dropping orders_customer_id_idx, add a covering index on (customer_id, created_at DESC) CONCURRENTLY so recent_orders_for_customer keeps using an index scan instead of a full table scan.

review.summary: The new index is on status but the report query filters on lower(status), so it still seq-scans all 2M rows after migration and gains nothing.
evidence: weekly_paid_report seq-scanned 2,000,001 rows both before (101ms) and after (99ms) the migration
concurrent writer stall was fine (max 2ms) so the index build itself is not the problem
fix verified: expression index on lower(status), created_at dropped seq-scanned rows to 0 and execution time to 13ms
review.fixed_migration: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_status_lower_created_idx ON orders (lower(status), created_at) WHERE lower(status) = 'paid';
review.action: Replace the plain status index with the expression index matching lower(status) (optionally partial on 'paid') before merging.

review.summary: ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN notes SET NOT NULL fails outright because ~90% of existing rows have NULL notes, so the migration never completes.
evidence: Simulation returned error: column "notes" of relation "orders" contains null values
Seed data has ~90% NULL notes (only rows with random()<0.1 get a value) causing the constraint to be violated on existing rows
Fixed version (batched backfill + NOT VALID/VALIDATE/SET NOT NULL) completed in 3.7s wall time with longest single transaction only 90ms and writer stall 6ms
review.action: Backfill NULL notes in small batched transactions, validate a NOT VALID check constraint, then apply SET NOT NULL instead of running the bare ALTER on populated data.
